subject: Re: urgent — NimbusRetail p99 jump / short-term bridge + roadmap asks
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ops Nimbus <ops@nimbusretail.com>, Alice Wu <alice.wu@nimbusretail.com>
Date: Sat, 6 Jun 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: NimbusRetail — sudden p99 and throughput dip (US-WEST-2)

Team — heads up. Monitoring flagged a sustained p99 jump in gen-api for NimbusRetail (us-west-2) starting ~07:45 PDT. Symptoms: p50 ~ 120ms -> 160ms (minor), p95 ~ 480ms -> 1.1s, p99 ~ 620ms -> 2.2s, and observed throughput drop ~28% on their traffic slice. Errors are still low (5xx < 0.1%), but tail latency is impacting interactive workflows.

Attached: latency_graph_us-west-2_20260606.png and request_samples_06-06.jsonl (sampled requests around spike).

Initial asks: 
- Ben / SRE: quick triage and immediate mitigations we can flip (routing, queue limits, caching hints).
- Marissa / Product: any config flags we can expose short-term to customers (prefetch/batching defaults, per-req token caps) and longer-term roadmap tradeoffs.
- Jonas / Infra: if this looks like kernel-scheduling or autoscaler thrash, what's the safe emergency rollback/route?

Customer comms: Ops Nimbus is copied and asked for patience while we investigate. They want a short status note we can share with their PM by EOD. I sketched a one-paragraph apology below — please iterate.

DRAFT CUSTOMER LINE (please edit):
"We’re seeing higher-than-normal latency for a subset of requests in US-WEST-2; our engineering teams are actively investigating and have deployed temporary routing changes to stabilize latency while we identify a longer-term fix. We expect to have an update within 4 hours."

I’ll host a 30-minute bridge at 09:00 PDT if we need it. If we can contain triage over email/slack, call it out.

-Neha

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ops Nimbus <ops@nimbusretail.com>
Date: Sat, 6 Jun 2026 09:16:00 -0700
Subject: Re: NimbusRetail — sudden p99 and throughput dip (US-WEST-2)

Quick triage notes from SRE after initial sweep: 
- Root/likely cause: autoscaler oscillation on a subset of pods serving a heavy tail of long-token requests. We see frequent scale-up -> scale-down cycles which cause KV cache churn and increase cold-start latencies for long contexts.
- Evidence: correlated spikes coincident with requests > 8k tokens in the sample set (see request_samples_06-06.jsonl).

Immediate mitigations I can flip now (minutes):
1) Enforce a soft per-request token cap of 6k for the gen-api route for NimbusTraffic. This will reject/redirect extremely long requests rather than let them monopolize inference workers.
2) Enable queue isolation (reserve 10% capacity for small/interactive requests) — reduces head-of-line blocking.
3) Warm KV cache heuristic: pin active prefixes on a small warm pool for 30m.
4) Route heavy requests to a lower-priority pool with longer allowed latency (if customer OK).

I attached a short customer note draft (cust_note_draft.md) that says what we flipped and the next steps. Recommend we execute 1+2 immediately and hold on 4 until we discuss with product.

I’ll stand by in #bridge-nimbus on Slack. If we go to emergency dedicated routing we need an ops lead to execute and I need a quick thumbs-up from product to adjust customer-visible limits.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ops Nimbus <ops@nimbusretail.com>
Date: Sat, 6 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: NimbusRetail — sudden p99 and throughput dip (US-WEST-2)

Thanks, Ben — that triage matches my read from the perf traces. A few product/roadmap notes: 
- Short-term: I agree with #1 and #2. We should make the per-req cap configurable per-account so we can avoid user-visible rejects for customers that need long requests (but default to safer bounds).
- Medium-term (roadmap ask): we need work in two areas: (a) smarter kernel scheduling to avoid thrash when mixed short/long requests are co-located; (b) fine-grained KV cache eviction + active prefix pinning exposed as a policy. I’m proposing we prioritize INF-9204 (kernel scheduling improvement) and INF-9205 (kv cache policy) in the next sprint.

I filed INF-9204 and linked it here: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/INF-9204. Will create INF-9205 now.

Customer messaging: Ben, I updated cust_note_draft.md with the mitigations and a brief timeline. Suggest we send a short note to Ops Nimbus now that 1+2 are approved and flipped, and follow up with an internal postmortem within 48 hours.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Product Operations, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Ops Nimbus <ops@nimbusretail.com>, Alice Wu <alice.wu@nimbusretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 6 Jun 2026 14:37:00 -0700
Subject: Update: stabilizing actions taken for latency spike (US-WEST-2)

Hi Alice / Nimbus ops — quick update from our side: 

We identified a tail of very long requests that was causing autoscaler instability and cache churn in the cluster serving your traffic. Our SRE team has taken the following temporary actions to stabilize latency: 
- Enforced a per-request soft token cap (6k tokens) for the affected route to prevent single requests from monopolizing capacity.
- Activated queue isolation to reserve capacity for short/interactive requests.
- Pinned active prefixes to a warm pool for 30 minutes to reduce cold cache penalties.

Early signals look positive — p99 has dropped from ~2.2s to ~850ms in the sampled window. We will continue observation and share a follow-up within 4 hours with more details and any next steps. We will not discard requests that need longer contexts without a follow-up with your team — if you have workflows that require >6k tokens we can route those to a lower-priority lane or discuss an account-level exception.

Thanks for your patience — looping Ben and Marissa for the next steps and postmortem cadence.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Sr. Product Manager, Redwood Inference
